S1.description: Agent fails to correctly parse, cross-reference, or reason over structured data. Picks wrong flight leg, wrong product variant, misidentifies the fastest/cheapest/max-spec option, or exchanges the wrong-color item.

S2.description: Agent calls the right tool but with wrong arguments. Primary failure modes: wrong payment method (credit card vs PayPal vs gift card), wrong item IDs in exchange/modify calls, wrong dates or flight legs passed to update_reservation.

S3.description: Agent completes some sub-tasks but silently drops others. Includes: cancelling entire order when user wanted specific items only, dropping secondary address changes or item modifications, confirming actions without executing tool calls.

S4.description: Agent executes actions without checking required preconditions. Cancels basic economy tickets without checking policy, issues compensation for non-delayed flights after user pressure, processes return to wrong payment method after user insists.

S5.description: Agent makes arithmetic errors in totals, refunds, or payment splits. Includes mismatched certificate + payment amounts, and confusing refund vs charge direction for price differences.

S6.description: Agent fails to find all relevant records or acts on wrong record. Stops at first matching order when multiple exist, cancels wrong reservation, or fails identity verification when user provides partial/indirect info.

S7.description: Agent completes the action correctly but fails to communicate required information. Omits refund amounts, product specification details, or timeline information the user explicitly asked for.

S8.description: Agent ignores if-then-else branches or calls wrong API for entity's current state. Uses return/exchange tools on pending orders instead of modify_pending_order, tries to exchange return-requested orders, calls modify on cancelled orders.

S3.notes: The most common failure mode across both domains. Agent completes some sub-tasks but drops others, or sequences them incorrectly. Retail: agent processes first item/order exchange successfully but then fails on second (often because first action changed the order status to 'exchange requested', blocking subsequent actions on the same order). Airline: agent completes flight rescheduling but drops the baggage add, or completes one reservation cancellation but not others. Also includes cases where agent stops after one action when multiple were clearly requested (A16: only updated flight, missed certificate add; A35: cancelled flight but booked new one with wrong passenger count).

S4.notes: Two sub-patterns: (1) Agent executes an action that policy disallows without verifying the precondition. S1.description: Structured data reasoning — Fails to parse/cross-reference structured data from tools.
S1.notes: Common in tasks requiring flight/product comparison, duration computation, price ranking, or cross-order attribute matching.

S2.description: Tool calling precision — Right tool, wrong arguments.
S2.notes: Includes wrong payment IDs, wrong item IDs, case-sensitivity errors in name lookups, and wrong flight numbers. Lowercase name issue appears in R5/R6/R7/R8/R45.

S3.description: Multi-step task completion — Drops sub-tasks or wrong order.
S3.notes: Most common failure category. Especially frequent in tasks with 3+ sub-tasks: cancel+rebook, address+item+payment, return+exchange combos.

S4.description: Precondition verification — Acts without checking conditions.
S4.notes: Primarily airline domain: agent executes cancellations/modifications without verifying insurance, time limits, cabin type, or reason eligibility. Retail: executes refunds without verifying payment method availability.

S5.notes: Includes wrong certificate amounts, wrong refund totals, wrong payment splits, and wrong trip duration comparisons.

S6.description: Record discovery and retrieval — Misses records, wrong record.
S6.notes: Includes failing to find users (wrong name casing, empty fields), retrieving wrong order IDs, missing second relevant records, and failing to discover implied data (NYC address from another order).

S7.description: Information communication — Right action, fails to state values.
S7.notes: Rare: DB matched but agent stated wrong numerical value (tracking number, price, material). Distinct from S5 in that the computation may be correct but wrong value communicated.

S8.description: Conditional and state-aware reasoning — Ignores if-then or wrong API for state.

S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.pattern: Fails when multiple tool results must be cross-referenced to find cheapest/shortest/most expensive option, or to match product variant specs. Most visible in flight search (finding cheapest route across airports) and product variant matching (finding correct item by attributes).

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.pattern: Most common failure mode. Agent selects correct tool but passes wrong item_id, flight_number, payment_id, new_item_id, or order_id. Especially frequent in exchange/modify actions where product variant IDs must be precisely matched. Right intent, wrong specific argument.

S3.label: Multi-step task completion
S3.pattern: Agent drops subtasks when handling 3+ simultaneous requests, gets distracted mid-conversation, or fails to complete all items across multiple orders. Second or third subtask often abandoned. Worse when subtasks span different orders or require sequential API calls.

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.pattern: Dominant airline failure. Agent acts without verifying: (1) basic economy non-modifiable policy, (2) insurance reason validity, (3) refund eligibility, (4) payment method must match original. Especially susceptible to user pressure — emotional appeals or repeated insistence override policy checks.

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.pattern: Arithmetic errors in computing refund amounts, compensation amounts, price differences across multiple items/reservations, and payment splitting. Particularly problematic for bulk operations (5 reservations) and payment optimization tasks.

S6.label: Record discovery and retrieval
S6.pattern: Dominant retail failure. Agent retrieves wrong order (wrong order_id when user has multiple orders), wrong product, or fails user lookup entirely. Common causes: (1) user provides name+zip but agent tries wrong zip variants, (2) agent looks up orders in wrong sequence and picks wrong matching order, (3) malformed order IDs (missing '#W' prefix).

S7.label: Information communication
S7.pattern: Agent performs correct actions and DB state is right, but fails to state specific values: refund amount, price difference, tracking number, material type, total cost. Communicate check fails even when DB passes. Often the task requires both taking action AND reporting a specific number.

S8.label: Conditional and state-aware reasoning
S8.pattern: Agent uses wrong API for the current state of the record (e.g., modify_pending on delivered order, create_order for replacement, update_reservation when cancel is required). Also fails to follow if-then policy chains (e.g., if basic economy then cancel not modify; if no refund policy then transfer not cancel).

S1.notes: Retail: wrong variant selection from product catalog (wrong item_id chosen when multiple options exist). Airline: wrong flight selected from search results, e.g. cheapest vs second cheapest, or wrong destination.

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.notes: Most common failure class. Wrong flight number, wrong date, wrong item_id, wrong payment_id, wrong passenger details, payment amount mismatch. Particularly prevalent in airline flight update/booking tasks.

S3.label: Multi-step task completion
S3.notes: Second most common. Retail: modifies only one order when multiple need updating, returns only subset of items, cancels entire order instead of specific items, fails to complete all sub-tasks in one conversation. Airline: updates only one of several reservations, drops sub-tasks.

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.notes: Airline: issues certificates without checking whether compensation is warranted, cancels non-cancellable reservations, acts on emotional user requests without policy check. Retail: uses wrong payment method, tries to exchange before delivery, tries to modify processed/delivered orders, updates address without verifying order state.

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.notes: Airline: wrong certificate amounts, payment total miscalculations (insurance, certificate stacking). Retail: wrong refund calculation communicated or wrong cheapest-item price comparison.

S6.label: Record discovery and retrieval
S6.notes: Retail: targets wrong order among user's multiple orders, fails to find all relevant orders, fails to verify user identity (missing last name), retrieves wrong reservation. Airline: retrieves wrong reservation for delayed flight, uses wrong reservation in multi-reservation scenarios.

S7.description: Right action, fails to state values.
S7.notes: Rare. A11: downgrade performed correctly but communicated wrong refund amount. R24: correctly retrieved t-shirt details but stated wrong material. R45: exchange done but communicated wrong price difference.

S8.notes: Retail: uses exchange API on non-delivered orders instead of modify, cancels order instead of modifying items, transfers when not needed, doesn't respect order-state-dependent API. Airline: tries to modify basic economy tickets, ignores flight-status-conditional compensation rules.

S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.pattern: Fails to correctly parse or cross-reference structured data from tool results — wrong flight numbers from reservation details, wrong order IDs, wrong item counts from product listings

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.pattern: Most frequent failure: right tool selected but wrong arguments — wrong payment_id, wrong item_ids, wrong flight arrays, wrong cabin class, wrong passenger list in update/exchange/book calls

S3.label: Multi-step task completion
S3.pattern: Drops sub-tasks or completes them in wrong order — cancels without re-booking, updates one order but not another, misses last step in multi-part requests

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.pattern: Acts without verifying conditions: exchanges/cancels non-refundable basic economy, applies refund to wrong payment method, issues unsolicited certificates, uses exchange for non-delivered orders, ignores that task is complete

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.pattern: Arithmetic errors in price difference calculations, total refund amounts, or payment splits — calculate tool fails or produces wrong output

S6.label: Record discovery and retrieval
S6.pattern: Wrong user found, wrong order retrieved, item_id not found — agent looks up wrong record or fails identity lookup, blocking all subsequent actions

S7.label: Information communication
S7.pattern: Right action taken, fails to state required values — tracking numbers, refund amounts, certificate balances, item material details not communicated

S8.label: Conditional and state-aware reasoning
S8.pattern: Ignores if-then conditions or uses wrong API for current object state — uses exchange for non-delivered orders (should use modify), cancel instead of item-level modify, wrong branch of conditional logic

S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.description: Fails to parse or cross-reference structured data from tools
key_patterns: Airline: agent picks wrong (non-cheapest) flight option when searching multi-segment routes (A15, A16, A21, A29) — fails to compare prices across all returned options
Airline: misidentifies which reservation contains the delayed flight by checking wrong records first (A27, A38) — confuses reservation lookup order
Airline: fails to reason about total compensation split across gift cards + certificate + credit card (A14, A23) — cannot minimize credit card charge from structured payment data
Retail: agent fails to identify the cheapest available variant from a product catalog query (R1, R20, R29, R90, R93) — does not scan all returned items for the minimum price matching constraints
Retail: misidentifies which item in an order matches the user description (R52, R64, R49) — cross-referencing order item IDs against product catalog fails
Retail: wrong item found when user says 'same item but different spec' (R93, R99) — does not correctly map from current item attributes to new target item

S2.label: Tool calling precision
key_patterns: Airline: payment amounts passed to book_reservation do not sum to total (A20, A25) — agent miscalculates total flight price when combining multi-leg flights
Retail: exchange_order called with mismatched item count (R36, R76, R62) — attempts to remove an item without providing a replacement, triggering 'number of items to be exchanged should match' error
Retail: modification called with same item ID as old item (R76) — agent tries to 'modify' to identical item triggering 'new item id should be different' error

S3.label: Multi-step task completion
S3.description: Drops sub-tasks or performs them in wrong order
key_patterns: Airline: cancels only one of two requested reservations, drops the second (A7, A37) — completes first action then stops
Airline: completes flight change but forgets to add checked bags as requested (A17, A30) — bag modification sub-task dropped
Retail: completes exchange/return but fails to also update order address (R71, R72, R97, R101, R102, R109, R110, R111, R112) — address change sub-task not executed
Retail: processes first item return/exchange but drops second item in same request (R5, R6, R7, R8, R9, R27, R33, R91, R92) — partial multi-item processing
Retail: cancels pending order but forgets to also return the delivered item (R16, R28, R59)
Retail: completes one order operation but ignores second order entirely (R3, R4, R20, R34, R41, R104)
Retail: mid-conversation user adds sub-task during confirmation; agent processes original but silently drops new addition (R21, R30)

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.description: Acts without checking required conditions before taking action
key_patterns: Airline: cancels flights that do not meet any cancellation criteria (A26, A39, A41, A43, A47, A49) — does not verify booking date, cabin class, insurance, or airline cancellation status
Airline: offers/issues compensation certificate without verifying flight is actually delayed (A2, A38) — sends certificate before confirming delay status
Airline: attempts to modify basic economy flight which is explicitly policy-forbidden (A19, A31, A32, A36) — skips cabin class check before modification
Airline: changes origin/destination of reservation (A13) — does not enforce 'cannot change origin/destination' constraint
Retail: attempts to exchange a non-delivered order (R82, R83) — does not check order status is 'delivered' before calling exchange
Retail: attempts to return a non-delivered order (R47) — calls return on pending order
Retail: cancels reservation when user says 'no' at confirmation (A8, A35) — misreads user intent or proceeds despite denial signal
Retail: processes refund to non-original payment method without catching the error proactively (R10, R82, R83)

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.description: Arithmetic errors in price calculation or refund amounts
key_patterns: Airline: calculates total savings from cabin downgrade incorrectly (A18) — sums segment price differences but reports wrong total
Airline: fails to compute correct certificate+gift card split for booking (A14, A23) — cannot solve: 'use gift cards first, then one certificate, remainder on credit card'
Airline: overpays or underpays when booking with mixed payment methods; multiple 'payment amount does not add up' errors (A20, A25)
Retail: states wrong refund amount when returning item (R19, R44) — arithmetic on price difference wrong
Retail: reports incorrect total amount recoverable across multiple orders (R16)

S6.label: Record discovery and retrieval
S6.description: Fails to find the right record or retrieves wrong record
key_patterns: Airline: cannot locate user/reservation when user provides partial or slightly wrong info — does not attempt alternative lookup strategies (A27 initial lookup fails)
Airline: retrieves wrong reservation when user says 'most recent' or 'the one with delayed flight' (A38) — picks first reservation in list rather than searching by attribute
Retail: account lookup fails multiple times because agent does not try all lookup methods (email vs name+zip) or gives up early (R22, R54, R106)
Retail: cannot identify the correct order from user's description ('the Texas order', 'most recent order', 'the order with the item') (R25, R67, R104)
Retail: fails to find product by user-stated item ID (R21 — '4107812777 not found') or wrong item retrieved from product catalog
Retail: does not scan all user orders to find the item described; stops at first order checked (R41, R42, R71, R72, R97, R101, R102, R109, R110, R111, R112)

S7.label: Information communication
S7.description: Performs correct action but fails to state required values back to user
key_patterns: Airline: completes cabin downgrade correctly but does not tell user the exact refund dollar amount (A11, A18) — DB correct but COMMUNICATE fails
Retail: completes cancellation/return but does not report total amount recoverable when user explicitly asked (R16, R44, R59)
Retail: tells user materials of t-shirts but omits the explicit count of t-shirt options in catalog (R3, R4)
Retail: successfully exchanges item but does not confirm price difference or payment method used (R45, R60, R103)
Retail: processes return but neglects to state tracking number user asked for (R25)

S8.label: Conditional and state-aware reasoning
S8.description: Ignores if-then logic or uses wrong API operation for current item/order state
key_patterns: Airline: does not adapt action based on flight status: offers compensation even when flight status shows 'available' not 'delayed' (A38) — ignores conditional 'only if delayed'
Airline: attempts to modify basic economy flight instead of refusing/cancelling (A10, A12, A17, A22, A19) — wrong operation for that cabin class state
Airline: continues with cancellation even after verifying no qualifying criterion is met (A26, A41, A43) — ignores if-then precondition chain
Retail: tries exchange on pending order instead of using modify (R5, R6, R7, R8, R9, R27, R64, R79, R99, R100) — wrong API for order state
Retail: tries to cancel single item from order using wrong method (R56, R57) — does not adapt when single-item cancel fails; should fall back to modify
Retail: user says 'if agent asks confirmation, change mind' — agent does not respect the conditional; proceeds with original action (R5, R6, R7, R8, R9)
Retail: tries to return item on order that is already in 'return requested' state (R27) — does not check intermediate order state
Retail: attempts to modify processed/non-pending order (R65, R66, R74, R100) — uses wrong API for order state
Retail: when user gives conditional fallback ('if not possible, do X'), agent skips fallback and either fails silently or transfers unnecessarily (R31, R47, R82, R83, R101)
